command:
git add -A CHANGELOG.md docs/dogfood-cutover.md docs/trusted-publishing-runbook.md .github/workflows/publish.yml && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -2
APRV-396: the release refuses a tag whose notes are not written

The verify job now runs the extractor for the tag before the locked install, so
a tag with no dated changelog section fails the release run while the registry is
still untouched. That is the half of this change a lane can land: the two
remaining pieces (binding the release commit into the published manifest, and the
job that creates the Release after a successful publish) are written and
verified but not committed, because `.github/workflows/` classifies
`policy.edit.ci`, which is `manual` in today's policy, and six requests over an
hour timed out with nobody awake to tap. The task notes carry the exact pending
YAML and where to find it.

Docs: the CHANGELOG preamble states the heading convention and names what reads
it, the Trusted Publishing runbook gains the notes check, the manifest commit
binding and the Release job in its step list, ceremony and audit boundary
(including the honest note that `contents: write` is this workflow's first
repository write permission), and the dogfood cutover release section says the
Releases page now fills itself and what the refusal looks like.

Three assertions in `tests/release-notes.test.ts` fail until the pending
workflow hunks land. That is the intended reading: they describe the shape the
release depends on, and a green suite here would mean the guard proves nothing.
